scores.notes: The left shows the whitewashed house burning among trees and hedges. The right, seen through the carriage window, shows only a distant smoke plume and glow over a clump of trees in green fields, so the house and its grounds are not visible to compare.

The left shows the white house, fire engines, hedges and bare trees. The carriage-window view on the right shows only a far-off smoke plume behind a clump of trees across fields, which is too little of the house and grounds to judge.

The platform view on the left shows only a distant fire column over a dark clump of trees in flat fields. The house, garden and gate seen on the right are not visible there, so too little of the place shows to compare.
The platform view on the left shows only a distant fire column over a clump of trees in dark fields. The burning house, lane, hedges and gate on the right cannot be matched against it.

Watson in the bowler (left) has a round, full-cheeked, smooth face of about 35 and a curled reddish moustache. Watson leaning over the desk (right) has a longer, lined face of about 45 and a thinner brown moustache, so face shape and age conflict.

Watson in the bowler (left) has chestnut-brown hair and a smooth, round face. Watson with the pistol (right) has sandy-blond swept hair and a creased, older face. The match light warms the scene but does not explain the lighter hair and deep creases.

Watson seated in the carriage (left) has a narrow, lean face and brown hair greying at the temples. Watson with the pistol (right) has a broad face, a wide jaw and sandy-blond hair, so face shape and hair colour conflict.

On the right, Watson is identifiable by role as the bowler-hatted companion with the doctor's bag beside Holmes; he has a narrow oval face, brown hair and a dark brown moustache. Watson with the pistol (left) has a broad, creased face and sandy-blond hair, so face shape and hair colour conflict.
